Explain the characteristics of: • public sector organisations • private sector organisations • sole traders • partnerships.
Explain the connection between stakeholders and a business, identifying the stakeholders’ use of the business’s financial statements.
Understand the significance of the following accounting concepts: • consistency • prudence • accruals • materiality • money measurement • business entity.
Explain the benefits of using technology within accounting: • accounting software • spreadsheets.
Explain the issues regarding the security of data: • data loss • access • confidentiality.
Explain the methods of protecting data: • hardware • software.

Apply the principles of professional ethics to accounting roles and functions.

Explain why it is necessary to provide a provision for irrecoverable debts.
Distinguish between an irrecoverable debt and a provision for an irrecoverable debt.
Calculate and record irrecoverable debts and provision for irrecoverable debts in the books of account.
Explain why it is necessary to account for other receivables and payables.
Distinguish between other receivables and payables.
Calculate and record other receivables and payables in the books of account.
Students are assessed through a 2-hour written examination, set and marked
The examination comprises a mixture of multiple-choice, short- and long-answer
Section A comprises 10 1-mark multiple-choice questions and three short-answer
Section B comprises five multi-part questions worth 15 marks each.
The total number of marks available for the examination paper is 100.
The examination addresses all three Assessment Objectives.**
Externally assessed 33.3% of the total International GCSE
Availability: January and June
First assessment: June 2019
Explain the purpose of a trial balance.
Prepare a trial balance.
Understand the limitations of a trial balance.
Explain the purpose of control accounts.
Prepare a trade receivables control account and a trade payables control account.
Identify and explain errors that do and do not affect the balancing of the trial balance.
Prepare journal entries to correct errors.
Prepare a suspense account.
Explain the purpose of bank reconciliation statements.
Understand the process of bank reconciliation.
Prepare a bank reconciliation statement.
